title: AI inference gateway

milestones.title: [P6.1] Inference gateway: contracts, mock backend, and cancellable token streaming
milestones.task: Implement the generator contract and close propagation. Consume one token, then explicitly close the stream as a disconnected HTTP/SSE transport would. Use try/finally so provider cleanup and accounting run during generator cancellation.
milestones.failureInjection: A abandoned generator that remains referenced may retain a reservation. The transport adapter must close on disconnect; documentation and tests should show that ownership contract.
milestones.evidence: Observe one delivered token, cancelled outcome, zero active count, and charge of exactly one illustrative output unit.
milestones.testCommand: py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P6_1 -v
milestones.stopCondition: Stop when the focused deterministic test passes and the stated evidence is recorded. Extensions are separate practice.

milestones.title: [P6.2] Inference gateway: tenant admission, token limits, and budgets
milestones.task: Under a lock, reserve max_tokens and one concurrency slot before advancing the provider. Start a stream for Alice, reject her second concurrent stream, and allow Bob independently. Release unused budget when the stream ends.
milestones.failureInjection: Checking balance and decrementing in separate critical sections permits over-admission. Reserving only delivered tokens can also permit too many simultaneous future obligations.
milestones.evidence: Demonstrate tenant isolation and deterministic rejection when the requested ceiling exceeds remaining allowance.
milestones.testCommand: py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P6_2 -v
milestones.stopCondition: Stop when the focused deterministic test passes and the stated evidence is recorded. Extensions are separate practice.

milestones.title: [P6.3] Inference gateway: provider failures, cancellation, and telemetry
milestones.task: Inject a disconnect after one token and a provider delay past the deadline. Guarantee finally cleanup, distinguish provider_error from timeout/cancelled, and avoid automatic stream retries once output has been observed.
milestones.failureInjection: Retrying a partially delivered generation can duplicate or contradict visible output. State whether a client should start a new logical request instead of hiding the failure.
milestones.evidence: Verify no reservation leak after provider error or timeout, with accurate emitted-unit count and terminal status.
milestones.testCommand: py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P6_3 -v
milestones.stopCondition: Stop when the focused deterministic test passes and the stated evidence is recorded. Extensions are separate practice.

milestones.title: [P6.4] Inference gateway: load/fault tests and latency/cost evidence
milestones.task: Run ten deterministic stub requests and total the output units. Compare first-token latency with overall duration. Label cost units and timing as simulation output; do not translate them into GPU capacity or vendor currency without a real measurement model.
milestones.failureInjection: Counting only completed requests conceals partial outputs and cancelled work. Include those outcomes separately and explain that real provider billing may count tokens not delivered to the client.
milestones.evidence: Provide per-request telemetry, 30 emitted units across ten runs, 0.02-second first-token simulation, and an explicit uncertainty/limitation paragraph.
milestones.testCommand: py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P6_4 -v
milestones.stopCondition: Stop when the focused deterministic test passes and the stated evidence is recorded. Extensions are separate practice.

baselineArtifact: Streaming gateway, tenant budgets, failure controls, observability
authorship: original prepared teaching implementation; curriculum names and milestone IDs source-derived
invariant: Admission atomically reserves each tenant’s maximum output-unit budget before work starts. Completion, cancellation and failure release unused reservations and preserve per-request accounting.
requirements: Expose a bounded streaming generator backed by an explicit local deterministic token stub.
Isolate tenant concurrency and output-unit budgets; reject reused request IDs rather than silently double-charge or replay incomplete streams.
Record delivery-unit counts, time to first delivered token, duration, and outcome; release reservations on every terminal path.
architecture: tenant + request ID → atomic concurrency/budget reservation → cancellable stub iterator → delivered token stream → finally release unused units + telemetry.
limitations: No AI model runs here. Stub tokens are illustrative output units, not tokenizer IDs, provider billing or measured inference throughput. Budgets are process-local. Deadline checks occur between cooperative stub tokens and cannot interrupt an arbitrary blocking provider call; real adapters need cancellable I/O and provider-side billing reconciliation.
extensions: Add a durable reservation ledger and crash reconciliation with conservative orphan handling.
Add a real cancellable HTTP adapter against a local fake SSE server, without a paid provider.
referenceReveal: Explicit reveal in the academy; reference source also remains inspectable on disk. Educational spoiler control, not secure examination.
